children: President Donald Trump's administration on Friday agreed to pull back open-ended permission for federal agencies to lay off employees during government shutdowns to settle a lawsuit by a group of unions.
The unions sued in October 2025 in the early days of what became the longest government shutdown in US history
A federal judge in San Francisco blocked more than 4,000 planned layoffs while the case played out
Under the settlement, guidance directing agencies to initiate mass layoffs during shutdowns will be abandoned
Agencies will remove blanket authorization for layoffs from their individual shutdown plans and give 30 days' notice if they intend to modify those plans
The Trump administration's campaign to downsize the federal government through mass layoffs and buyouts led the civilian workforce to shrink by ‌12% between September 2024 and January 2026

"This settlement places limits on [the administration's] ability to use federal workers as bargaining chips to push their extreme agenda during the next government shutdown," said Patrick Moran, president of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees
The case is American Federation of Government Employees v. Office of Management and Budget, US. District Court for the Northern District of California, No. 3:25-cv-8302.
For the unions: Danielle Leonard and Alice Wang of Altshuler Berzon; Norm Eisen and Craig Becker from Democracy Defenders Fund; Rushab Sanghvi of AFGE
For the Trump administration: Andrew Bernie of the US Department of Justice
